title: Thus he dwells contemplating the body as a body internally; or he dwells contemplating the body as a body externally; or he dwells contemplating the…
content: Thus he dwells contemplating the body as a body internally; or he dwells contemplating the body as a body externally; or he dwells contemplating the body as a body both internally and externally. Or he dwells contemplating the nature of arising in the body; or he dwells contemplating the nature of passing away in the body; or he dwells contemplating the nature of both arising and passing away in the body. 'There is a body,' mindfulness is established in him to the extent necessary for knowledge and mindfulness. And he dwells independent, not clinging to anything in the world. Bhikkhus, that is how a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body.

title: Brahmin, what do you think? Here, if a consecrated Khattiya king were to assemble a hundred people of various lineages and say: 'Come, those of…
content: Brahmin, what do you think? Here, if a consecrated Khattiya king were to assemble a hundred people of various lineages and say: 'Come, those of you born in Khattiya families, in brahmin families, of royal birth — bring the upper part of a fire-making stick made of saka wood, sala wood, salala wood, sandalwood, or lotus wood, and turn it to produce fire and heat. And those of you born in low families, in hunter families, in bamboo-weaver families, in cart-maker families, in scavenger families — bring the upper part of a fire-making stick made of a dog-trough, a pig-trough, a laundry trough, or dry castor-oil wood, and turn it to produce fire and heat.' — Brahmin, what do you think? Does only the fire produced and the heat generated by those born in Khattiya families, brahmin families, of royal birth, have flame, color, and light, and can that fire be used for fire's purposes? And does the fire produced and the heat generated by those born in low families... have no flame, no color, no light, and cannot be used for fire's purposes?" — "No, Master Gotama. The fire produced and the heat generated by those born in Khattiya families, brahmin families, of royal birth — that fire has flame, color, and light, and can be used for fire's purposes. And the fire produced and the heat generated by those born in low families, hunter families, bamboo-weaver families, cart-maker families, scavenger families — that fire also has flame, color, and light, and can be used for fire's purposes. All fire has flame, color, and light, and all fire can be used for fire's purposes." — "So too, brahmin, if a person from a Khattiya family goes forth... he can attain the right path, the wholesome Dhamma. If a person from a brahmin family... from a vessa family... from a sudda family goes forth... he can attain the right path, the wholesome Dhamma.

title: Standing to one side, the devata Candimasa spoke this verse before the Blessed One: They will go safely, Like deer in a mosquito-free zone, Having…
content:
Standing to one side, the devata Candimasa spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

They will go safely,
Like deer in a mosquito-free zone,
Having attained jhāna,
One-pointed, mindful, aware,
They will reach the far shore,
Like fish breaking a net,
Having attained jhāna,
Self-controlled, beyond faults.

title: - When the mind is sluggish, bhikkhus, that is not the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the concentration…
content: - When the mind is sluggish, bhikkhus, that is not the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the concentration enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the equanimity enlightenment factor. Why is that? Because when the mind is sluggish, bhikkhus, it is hard to arouse the mind with these things. Just as, bhikkhus, a person who wants to kindle a small fire, if he throws wet grass, wet cow-dung, and wet wood onto it, exposes it to rain and wind, and scatters dust on it, could he kindle that small fire?" - "No, Venerable Sir." - "So too, bhikkhus, when the mind is sluggish, that is not the time to cultivate the tranquility enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the concentration enlightenment factor, not the time to cultivate the equanimity enlightenment factor. Why is that? Because when the mind is sluggish, it is hard to arouse the mind with these things.

title: Bhikkhus, then Prince Vipassī asked the renunciant: 'Venerable sir, what have you done, that your head is not like others' heads, and your robe is…
content: Bhikkhus, then Prince Vipassī asked the renunciant: 'Venerable sir, what have you done, that your head is not like others' heads, and your robe is not like others' robes?' 'Your Highness, I am a renunciant.' 'Venerable sir, what is meant by a renunciant?' 'Your Highness, I am called a renunciant because I live well the holy life, live well the pure life, do good deeds, do meritorious deeds, refrain from harming living beings, have loving-kindness towards living beings.' 'Venerable sir, excellent is your renunciation, excellent is the well-lived holy life, the well-lived pure life, the doing of good deeds, the doing of meritorious deeds, the refraining from harming living beings, the having of loving-kindness towards living beings.'

title: Then the Blessed One, knowing it was Māra, spoke this verse to Māra: Whatever forms there be, In this world or the next, With excellent…
content:
Then the Blessed One, knowing it was Māra, spoke this verse to Māra:

Whatever forms there be,
In this world or the next,
With excellent color,
Shining in the sky,
All those forms
Praised by Māra,
Are merely bait
Thrown out to catch fish.

title: He again takes hold of internal contact and considers: 'But this craving, where does it arise, where does it settle?' He, taking hold of internal…
content: He again takes hold of internal contact and considers: 'But this craving, where does it arise, where does it settle?' He, taking hold of internal contact, knows: 'Whatever in the world is agreeable and enticing — there craving arises, there craving settles. And what in the world is agreeable and enticing? The eye in the world is agreeable and enticing — there craving arises, there craving settles.' ... The ear in the world ... the nose in the world ... the tongue in the world ... the body in the world ... the mind in the world is agreeable and enticing — there craving arises, there craving settles.

title: Bhikkhus, devas and humans delight in form, are excited by form. When form changes, fades away, and ceases, bhikkhus, devas and humans live in suffering.…
content: Bhikkhus, devas and humans delight in form, are excited by form. When form changes, fades away, and ceases, bhikkhus, devas and humans live in suffering. They delight in sound ... in odor ... in taste ... in touch ... Bhikkhus, devas and humans delight in mind-objects, are excited by mind-objects. When mind-objects change, fade away, and cease, bhikkhus, devas and humans live in suffering. Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, having truly understood the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape regarding form, does not delight in form, does not enjoy form, is not excited by form. When form changes, fades away, and ceases, bhikkhus, the Tathāgata lives in happiness. He does not delight in sound ... in odor ... in taste ... in touch ... Having truly understood the arising, the passing away, the gratification, the danger, and the escape regarding mind-objects, the Tathāgata does not delight in mind-objects, does not enjoy them, is not excited by them. When mind-objects change, fade away, and cease, the Tathāgata lives in happiness.

title: I declare to you, bhikkhus, I make known to you, bhikkhus: For an immoral person, of evil character, impure, it would be better to have…
content:
I declare to you, bhikkhus, I make known to you, bhikkhus: For an immoral person, of evil character, impure, it would be better to have a strong man take a red-hot iron plate, blazing, flaming, and wrap it around his body. Why is that? Because, bhikkhus, from that cause he might meet death or death-like suffering, but not because of that cause, after death, with the breakup of the body, would he be reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. But when an immoral person, of evil character, impure in conduct... impure, enjoys the robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites offered out of faith by wealthy nobles, wealthy brahmins, or wealthy householders, then, bhikkhus, that leads to his long-term harm and suffering, and after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell.
Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: 'When we enjoy the requisites such as robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites of those donors, may our conduct be of great fruit and great benefit. And may our going forth not be in vain, but fruitful and rewarding.' Thus, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves.

title: 'The removal of greed, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion,' Venerable Sir, is thus said. What is the synonym for the removal of…
content: 'The removal of greed, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion,' Venerable Sir, is thus said. What is the synonym for the removal of greed, the removal of hatred, the removal of delusion?" - "It is a synonym for the Nibbāna element, bhikkhu, and is also called the destruction of the taints." When this was said, that bhikkhu said: "'The Deathless, the Deathless,' Venerable Sir, is thus said. What is the Deathless, Venerable Sir? What is the path leading to the Deathless?" - "The destruction of greed, the destruction of hatred, the destruction of delusion, bhikkhu, is called the Deathless. This Noble Eightfold Path is the path leading to the Deathless, that is, right view ... right concentration.
